extracted.intended_audience: researchers and community members who want to request, write, or engage with peer reviews of preprints (including early-career researchers and community organizers)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and criteria for requesting, performing, and displaying peer reviews of preprints on the PREreview platform, including rapid (12-question) and long-form reviews, reviewer eligibility, transparency, and interaction rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid review (12-question form)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fill out and submit a rapid review—12 yes/no/not sure/n.a. questions designed to capture the essence of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid reviews are aggregated and displayed next to the preprint to give a concise snapshot of the paper; questions use yes/no/not sure/n.a. options to standardize quick assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-form review (solo or collaborative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compose a long-form review on a preprint, alone or in collaboration with other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form reviews allow extended critique and can be written collaboratively; they are displayed alongside rapid reviews and the preprint. Users can comment on others’ reviews and engage in discussion about long-form reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility: ORCID and Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone with an ORCID iD and willing to abide by our Code of Conduct may be an eligible reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users register with an ORCID iD and may use either a public or pseudonymous persona. Compliance with the platform's Code of Conduct is required (link provided on the site).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage: Complete paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Review coverage is listed as 'Complete paper'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are intended to address the complete manuscript rather than only abstracts or fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection: Self-nominated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers volunteer themselves rather than being appointed by editors; this emphasizes community-driven participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review requested by: Non-authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews (or review requests) are requested by non-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for review should come from community members other than the paper's authors, supporting independent appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction and author response policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Public interaction: Yes. Author response: No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community members may publicly interact with reviews (comment, endorse, flag), but authors are not provided a formal response mechanism on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency modalities (identity/reports/interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency attributes include 'Open identities', 'Open interaction', 'Open reports', and 'Single blind'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform lists multiple transparency modes: identities can be public or pseudonymous (ORCID-based); interaction and reports are openly viewable. The page also records 'single blind' as a listed transparency state (platform-level attributes may accommodate different practices).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity disclosure: known to editor/service
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity known to: Editor or service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While users may present public or pseudonymous personas, the platform records that reviewer identities are known to the editor or platform service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests: not included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform does not include a competing-interests field as part of the review metadata (per the listed attributes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of code or data: not provided
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of code or data: No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PREreview's listed scope does not include formal review of code or data accompanying the preprint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript hosting: not a preprint server; fetches metadata/PDF
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript hosting: No. PREreview is not a preprint server; it fetches the metadata and pdf (when openly licensed) of a preprint from other servers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The platform displays and links to preprints hosted elsewhere (e.g., fetched from Google Scholar) rather than hosting manuscripts itself; goal is to enable reviews for any preprint on any server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Badges and training criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Tags or badges: Yes. Criteria for inclusion: badges can be given to reviewers; for now badges exist for users who have gone through the Open Reviewers mentoring and training program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badges indicate participation or completion of PREreview training/mentoring programs and may be used to recognize reviewer qualifications on the platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction features: comment, endorse, flag, communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Platform features include: comment on others’ reviews; endorse others’ reviews via Plaudit; flag reviews as violating the Code of Conduct; engage with or start communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interaction tools are meant to support collaborative moderation, peer endorsement, and community-based review practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public accessibility of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone can search for preprints that have reviews or requests for reviews on the site and read/sort aggregated rapid and long-form reviews next to the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and aggregated summaries are openly accessible to site visitors, promoting transparency and discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision/result model: no editorial decision; other scale or rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision: Other scale or rating. Author response: No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews on PREreview do not produce formal editorial decisions; instead the platform uses other rating/scale mechanisms (e.g., rapid-review questions and endorsements) to communicate evaluation.
